name: Nuxe Huile Prodigieuse

lead:
Huile Prodigieuse ("Prodigious Oil") is a multi-use dry oil from the French cosmetics brand Nuxe, created in 1991 and marketed for use on the face, body and hair. According to French Wikipedia, more than 20 million bottles have been sold.
For appearance, oils like this are used to leave skin feeling softer and looking more glowing and to smooth the look of hair ends. No published studies examine this specific product.

paras: Users apply a small amount of oil by hand to skin or ends of hair, often after a bath or as a finishing step. Brand marketing describes it as multi-purpose, so some use it on face, body and hair from one bottle. This article does not give a regimen.
As with any cosmetic oil, fragrance or plant-oil sensitivity can cause irritation in some people.

chain: Plant-oil blend applied to skin or hair
Surface feels softer and looks glossier
Healthier-looking skin and smoother hair ends
angle.text: The oil is applied to skin and hair for a soft, glowing finish, as marketed by the brand. The effect is on surface appearance and lasts until the oil is washed off.

lead: Huile Prodigieuse is the signature product of Nuxe, a French cosmetics brand. French Wikipedia says Aliza Jabès founded the brand in 1989 and that the oil was created in 1991.[1]

The oil is marketed as a multi-purpose dry oil for face, body and hair, which makes it a one-product way to give skin a softer, more luminous look and hair a smoother finish. Wikipedia reports more than 20 million bottles sold.[1]
No published clinical studies of the product were identified.

paras: Aliza Jabès founded Nuxe in 1989, buying it back from a Parisian laboratory dating from 1957 that specialised in aromatherapy and herbal medicine; the infobox gives a conflicting 1964 company date. The Huile Prodigieuse was created in 1991.[1]
The brand presents it as a multi-use oil for face, body and hair.[1]

timeline.event: Aliza Jabès founds Nuxe as a brand.[1]
